response.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.position, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.position), shares AS (SELECT member_id, position, attendance_count, attendance_count * 1.0 / SUM(attendance_count) OVER () AS share FROM counts), ranked AS (SELECT member_id, position, attendance_count, share, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS rnk FROM shares) SELECT member_id, position, attendance_count, share FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY share DESC;

assumptions.assumption: Attendance is matched to members with an inner join on attendance.link_to_member = member.member_id, so attendance rows without a matching member are dropped before counting.
A member's position is taken from the member table. A NULL position forms its own group rather than being dropped.
Share is each (member_id, position) count divided by the sum of all such counts after the unmatched rows are dropped. The denominator is the total of all attendance records that matched a member.
RANK() on share is used so that every row tied with the 10th-ranked share is kept, giving more than 10 rows when there is a tie at the cutoff.
